transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I almost didn’t make the appointment, because I don’t want to sound dramatic. But what scared me was that I’ve been having thoughts like… it might be simpler if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that, truly, but the thought itself frightened me enough that I thought I should come in. Is that… the kind of thing I should tell you?
How long have you been feeling this way and having these thoughts?

I suppose… it’s been longer than I’d like to admit. About eight months, I think. It seemed to start after my brother’s health and behavior changed so suddenly. I kept telling myself I was just handling a difficult situation, but… yes, around eight months.
Can you describe how you’ve been feeling most days over the past few weeks? Have you noticed changes in things like your sleep, appetite, energy, or ability to enjoy activities you used to like?

I’m not sure I’d call it severe, exactly… I don’t want to overstate it. But most days lately it feels as if a sort of gray film has settled over everything. Even simple things, like making tea or looking out at my garden, feel… muted. There’s this quiet heaviness in me that I can’t quite reason my way out of, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, or a feeling of sadness that doesn’t go away?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I have noticed it with my watercolors. I still set everything out sometimes, the paper and paints, and then I just sit there looking at it. The feeling I used to get from the colors and the light… it just doesn’t seem to come. Then I put it all away. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or blaming yourself for things that you wouldn’t have thought were your fault before?

Yes… I suppose I have, though I know it may not be entirely rational. I keep going back over my brother’s decline and thinking, if I had been a better sister, or just more attentive, maybe I would have noticed sooner. Maybe I could have prevented some of it.

I know that probably sounds unfair to myself, doesn’t it? But it’s a thought I return to more than I’d like.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly lately, or that it takes you longer to get things done? Or on the flip side, have you felt restless or fidgety in ways you didn't used to?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that exactly. I mean, I’m probably not rushing about the way I used to, but I wouldn’t want to call it anything dramatic.

Some things may take me a bit longer, but I suppose that could just be… age, or being less busy now. I don’t think I’ve been especially fidgety or anything like that. Does that answer it properly?
Have you found yourself feeling worthless or like you’re a burden to others lately?

Maybe not worthless exactly… I don’t want to overstate it. But I do get caught in this loop about my brother. I keep telling myself that if I’d been a better sister, or more attentive, I might have noticed what was happening sooner and prevented some of it.

I know that may not be a fair way to think about it, but it does make me feel like I failed him somehow. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed that your movements or thoughts have slowed down, or that you're more restless or unable to stay still than usual?

I don’t think so, not in any clear way. I mean, I may be a bit slower getting going some days, but I haven’t noticed anything like being unable to move or think properly.

And I’m not especially restless, no… at least not that I’ve been aware of. I hope that answers what you’re asking.
Have you experienced any days where you felt physically slowed down or as though you were moving in slow motion, not just feeling tired but almost like it's hard to get your body to respond?

No, I don’t think I’ve had that exactly. Some mornings I’m slower to get started, but it feels more like ordinary tiredness or taking my time, not like my body won’t respond.

I haven’t felt like I’m moving in slow motion, at least not that I’ve noticed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed a loss of energy or felt fatigued more easily, even after doing things that wouldn’t normally tire you out?

I wouldn’t say it’s been a big problem, no. I do get tired sometimes, but at my age I suppose that’s not so unusual, and I haven’t really noticed becoming exhausted from things that normally wouldn’t bother me.

If anything, I might need to pace myself a little more, but I don’t think it’s a major change. Is that the kind of answer you mean?
Have you found that you’ve lost interest in most activities, even ones you used to enjoy, not just your watercolors?

Well… I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in everything, exactly. But with the watercolors, yes, that’s been the clearest thing.

I still set everything out sometimes, the brushes and paints, and then I just sort of sit there looking at the paper. The part I used to enjoy—the color, the light—it just doesn’t quite come. Then I end up putting it away again.

I don’t know if that counts as “most activities,” but that’s the main thing I’ve noticed.
Do you find that you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, or is there variation in how you feel throughout the day?

There is some variation, I suppose, but… most days there’s this sort of grayness over everything. Not dramatic, exactly, just a quiet heaviness.

Even when I’m doing something ordinary, like making tea or looking out at the garden, it’s still there in the background. I try to talk myself out of it, tell myself there’s no particular reason, but it doesn’t really lift the way I’d expect.

I don’t know if that sounds like what you’re asking about.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost everything you do, not just your watercolors, or is there still at least one activity that you find enjoyable or engaging?

I think… it’s mainly the watercolors that I notice. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

I do still get my things out sometimes—the paints and brushes—and I’ll sit there with the paper in front of me. But then I just stare at it for a while, and the pleasure I used to get from the colors and the light doesn’t really arrive. So I end up packing it all away.

I’m not sure I’d say it’s almost everything, though. Is that answering it properly?
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure not just in your watercolors, but in nearly all the activities you used to enjoy, even simple ones like spending time with loved ones or hobbies?

I’m not sure I’d say nearly all of them… I don’t want to overstate it.

The watercoloring is the one I keep noticing. I still sometimes put everything out—the paints, the brushes, the paper—and I think I’ll try. But then I just sit there looking at the blank page, and the pleasure I used to get from the colors and the light… it just doesn’t really come. After a while I pack it all away again.

So yes, there’s a loss of pleasure there, definitely. I’m just not sure I can fairly say it’s everything. Does that make sense?
Would you say that you feel down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day, even if it's not severe?

Yes… I think I would say that. I mean, it isn’t always severe, and I can still go through the motions of the day, so I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic.

But most days it does feel like there’s a kind of gray film over everything. Even when I’m just making tea or looking out at the garden, there’s this quiet heaviness in me. I try to reason myself out of it, but it doesn’t really go away.

Is that the sort of thing you mean?
